                  Given:

                  \n\n

                  If (X, Y) has a bivariate normal distribution, then X and Y are independent if and only if X and Y are uncorrelated.

                  \n\n

                  Concept:

                  \n\n

                  In a bivariate normal distribution, the independence of two variables (X and Y) implies that their covariance is zero, meaning they are uncorrelated.

                  \n\n

                  Relationship:

                  \n\n

                  Independence ⇒ Uncorrelated

                  \n\n

                  Uncorrelated does not necessarily imply independence, except in the case of a bivariate normal distribution.

                  \n\n

                  Formula Used:

                  \n\n

                  Cov(X, Y) = ρ(X, Y) × σX × σY

                  \n\n

                  Where:

                  \n\n
                    \n\t
                  • ρ(X, Y): Correlation coefficient
                    • \n\t
                  • σX, σY: Standard deviations of X and Y
                    • \n
                  \n\n

                  For independence:

                  \n\n

                  ρ(X, Y) = 0 ⇒ Cov(X, Y) = 0

                  \n\n

                  Calculation:

                  \n\n

                  ⇒ Independence of X and Y ⇒ ρ(X, Y) = 0

                  \n\n

                  ⇒ Cov(X, Y) = 0

                  \n\n

                  ⇒ X and Y are uncorrelated.

                  \n\n

                  Hence, for a bivariate normal distribution, X and Y are independent if and only if they are uncorrelated.

                  \n\n

                  ∴ The correct answer is Option 2: Uncorrelated.

                  ", "hn": "\n

                  यदि (X, Y) का एक द्विचर प्रसामान्य बंटन है, तो X और Y स्वतंत्र हैं यदि और केवल यदि X और Y असहसंबद्ध हैं।

                  एक द्विचर प्रसामान्य बंटन में, दो चरों (X और Y) की स्वतंत्रता का तात्पर्य है कि उनका सहप्रसरण शून्य है, जिसका अर्थ है कि वे असहसंबद्ध हैं।

                  \n\n

                  संबंध:

                  \n\n

                  स्वतंत्रता ⇒ असहसंबद्ध

                  \n\n

                  असहसंबद्धता का तात्पर्य आवश्यक रूप से स्वतंत्रता नहीं है, सिवाय द्विचर प्रसामान्य बंटन के मामले में।

                  \n\n

                  प्रयुक्त सूत्र:

                  \n\n

                  Cov(X, Y) = ρ(X, Y) x σX x σY

                  \n\n

                  कहाँ:

                  \n\n
                    \n\t
                  • ρ(X, Y): सहसंबंध गुणांक
                    • \n\t
                  • σX, σY: X और Y के मानक विचलन
                    • \n
                  \n\n

                  स्वतंत्रता के लिए:

                  \n\n

                  ρ(X, Y) = 0 ⇒ Cov(X, Y) = 0

                  \n\n

                  गणना:

                  \n\n

                  ⇒ X और Y की स्वतंत्रता ⇒ ρ(X, Y) = 0

                  \n\n

                  ⇒ Cov(X, Y) = 0

                  \n\n

                  ⇒ X और Y असहसंबद्ध हैं।

                  \n\n

                  ∴ सही उत्तर विकल्प 2: असहसंबद्ध है।

                    Binomial distribution: X ~ B(n, p)

                    \n\n

                    Concept:

                    \n\n

                    In a binomial distribution:

                    \n\n

                    Mean, μ = n × p

                    \n\n

                    Variance, σ² = n × p × (1 - p)

                    \n\n

                    Probability formula: P(X = k) = nCk × pk × (1 - p)n-k

                    \n\n

                    Formula Used:

                    \n\n

                    Mean: μ = n × p

                    \n\n

                    Variance: σ² = n × p × (1 - p)

                    \n\n

                    P(X = k) = nCk × pk × (1 - p)n-k

                    \n\n

                    Calculation:

                    \n\n

                    Step 1: Solve for n and p using mean and variance.

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ μ = n × p = 4

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ σ² = n × p × (1 - p) = 2

                    \n\n

                    Let p = probability of success.

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ n × p × (1 - p) = n × p - n × p²

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ Substitute μ = 4:

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ 4 × (1 - p) = 2

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ 4 - 4p = 2

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ 4p = 2

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ p = 0.5

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ Substitute p = 0.5 into μ = n × p:

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ 4 = n × 0.5

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ n = 8

                    \n\n

                    Step 2: Solve P(X = 2).

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ P(X = k) = nCk × pk × (1 - p)n-k

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ P(X = 2) = 8C2 × 0.52 × (1 - 0.5)8-2

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ P(X = 2) = 8C2 × 0.52 × 0.56

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ 8C2 = 8!/(2! × (8-2)!)

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ 8C2 = 8 × 7 / 2 = 28

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ P(X = 2) = 28 × 0.58

                    ⇒ 0.58 = 1/28

                    ⇒ P(X = 2) = 28 × 1/28

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ P(X = 2) = 28/256

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ P(X = 2) = 7/64

                    \n\n

                    ⇒ P(X = 2) = 7/26

                    \n\n

                    ∴ P(X = 2) = 7/26, which matches Option 2.

                        Given:

                        \n\n

                        Sample size (n) = 36

                        \n\n

                        Population mean (μ) = 2

                        \n\n

                        Population variance (σ2) = 25

                        \n\n

                        Sampling is done with replacement.

                        \n\n

                        Concept:

                        \n\n

                        The standard error of the sample mean (x̅) is calculated using the formula:

                        \n\n

                        Formula Used:

                        \n\n

                        Standard error (SE) = σ / √n

                        \n\n

                        where:

                        \n\n
                          \n\t
                        • σ = Population standard deviation (√variance)
                          • \n\t
                        • n = Sample size
                          • \n
                        \n\n

                        Calculation:

                        \n\n

                        Step 1: Calculate the population standard deviation (σ):

                        \n\n

                        ⇒ σ = √(variance) = √25 = 5

                        \n\n

                        Step 2: Calculate the standard error (SE):

                        \n\n

                        ⇒ SE = σ / √n

                        \n\n

                        ⇒ SE = 5 / √36

                        \n\n

                        ⇒ SE = 5 / 6

                        \n\n

                        Conclusion:

                        \n\n

                        ∴ The standard error of x̅ is 5/6.

                        \n\n

                        Hence, the correct answer is Option 3.

                        \n\n

                        ⇒ SE = σ / √n

                        The Correct Answer is: Residuals showing a skewed distribution

                        \n\n

                        Explanation

                        \n\n

                        In one-way ANOVA, the normality assumption means that the residuals (errors) are normally distributed.

                        \n\n

                        Let’s check each option:

                        \n\n

                        Equal variances across groups→ This relates to homogeneity of variance, not normality 

                        \n\n

                        Residuals showing a skewed distribution→ Skewness indicates the residuals are not normally distributed 

                        \n\n

                        \n\n

                        Independent observations→ This is a separate assumption (independence), not normality

                          \n\n

                          Mutually exclusive events: Two or more events are mutually exclusive if their intersection is empty, i.e., Ai ∩ Aj = Φ for i ≠ j.

                          Exhaustive events: Events are exhaustive if their union covers the entire sample space, i.e., UiAi = S.

                          \n\n

                          For events to be mutually exclusive and exhaustive, both properties must hold simultaneously.

                          \n\n

                          Option 2: States mutual exclusivity (Ai ∩ Aj = Φ for i ≠ j) but does not address exhaustive property. Incorrect.

                          \n\n

                          \n\n

                          Option 4: Combines UiAi = S (exhaustive) and Ai ∩ Aj = Φ for i ≠ j (mutual exclusivity). Correct.

                          दिया गया है:

                          \n\n

                          प्रतिदर्श समष्टि S में घटनाएँ Ai (i = 1, 2, 3, ...) हैं जो परस्पर अपवर्जी और नि:शेष हैं।

For a sample", "te": "", "mr": "", "bn": "", "ml": "", "gu": "", "kn": "", "ta": "", "or": "", "as": "", "ks": "", "kok": "", "mni": "", "ne": "", "pa": "", "sd": "", "ur": "", "sat": "", "mai": "", "brx": "", "doi": "", "sa": "", "grt": "", "kha": "", "lus": "", "bo": "", "trp": ""}, "tags": [], "concept": "Unidentified", "confidence": "unidentified"}, {"qid": "68400a905786631c7d552b89", "qs_no": 95, "pos_marks": 2.0, "neg_marks": 0.5, "type": "mcq", "langs": {"en": {"value": "If x̅ is the mean of a sample from N(μ, 1), then the maximum", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "n x̅<sup>2</sup>"}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "<span class="math-tex">\\(\\rm \\bar x^2+\\frac{1}{n}\\)</span>"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "x̅<sup>2</sup>&nbsp;+ 1"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "x̅<sup>2</sup>"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}, "hn": {"value": "यदि x̅, N(μ, 1) से एक प्रतिदर्श का माध्य है, तो अधिकतम", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "n x̅<sup>2</sup>"}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "<span class="math-tex">\\(\\rm \\bar x^2+\\frac{1}{n}\\)</span>"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "x̅<sup>2</sup> + 1"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "x̅<sup>2</sup>"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}}, "correct_option": "4", "solution_html": {"en": "\n

                            Given:

                            \n\n

                            If x̅ is the mean of a sample from N(μ, 1), then the maximum value of E(x̅²) is queried.

                            \n\n

                            Concept:

                            \n\n

                            E(x̅²) represents the expected value of the square of the sample mean. For a sample mean x̅ from N(μ, σ²), the variance of x̅ is σ²/n. Here σ = 1.

                            \n\n

                            E(x̅²) can be expressed as:

                            \n\n

                            E(x̅²) = Var(x̅) + (E(x̅))²

                            \n\n

                            Formula Used:

                            \n\n

                            Var(x̅) = σ²/n

                            \n\n

                            E(x̅) = μ

                            \n\n

                            Thus, E(x̅²) = (μ²) + (σ²/n)

                            \n\n

                            Calculation:

                            \n\n

                            Given the standard deviation σ = 1:

                            \n\n

                            ⇒ Var(x̅) = (1²)/n = 1/n

                            \n\n

                            ⇒ E(x̅) = μ

                            \n\n

                            ⇒ E(x̅²) = μ² + (1/n)

                            \n\n

                            Substituting μ = x̅ (mean of the sample):

                            \n\n

                            ⇒ E(x̅²) = x̅² + (1/n)

                            \n\n

                            Maximum value occurs when μ = x̅ and n → ∞ (large sample size). Therefore, the correct option is:

                            \n\n

                            ⇒ E(x̅²) = x̅²

                            \n\n

                            ∴ The correct answer is Option 4.

                            \n\nc6:T8e8,\n

                            &", "hn": "\n

                            दिया गया है:

                            \n\n

                            यदि x̅, N(μ, 1) से एक प्रतिदर्श का माध्य है, तो E(x̅²) का अधिकतम मान पूछा गया है।

                            \n\n

                            अवधारणा:

                            \n\n

                            E(x̅²) प्रतिदर्श माध्य के वर्ग के अपेक्षित मान को दर्शाता है। N(μ, σ²) से प्रतिदर्श माध्य x̅ के लिए, x̅ का प्रसरण σ²/n है। यहाँ σ = 1 है।

                            \n\n

                            E(x̅²) को इस प्रकार व्यक्त किया जा सकता है:

                            \n\n

                            E(x̅²) = Var(x̅) + (E(x̅))²

                            \n\n

                            प्रयुक्त सूत्र:

                            \n\n

                            Var(x̅) = σ²/n

                            \n\n

                            E(x̅) = μ

                            \n\n

                            इस प्रकार, E(x̅²) = (μ²) + (σ²/n)

                            \n\n

                            गणना:

                            \n\n

                            दिया गया मानक विचलन σ = 1:

                            \n\n

                            ⇒ Var(x̅) = (1²)/n = 1/n

                            \n\n

                            ⇒ E(x̅) = μ

                            \n\n

                            ⇒ E(x̅²) = μ² + (1/n)

                            \n\n

                            \n\n

                            ⇒ E(x̅²) = x̅²

                            \n\n

                                Calculation:

                                Efficiency of one sampling method with respect to another is defined as the ratio of their variances for the same estimator.

                                For estimating the population mean:

                                \n\n

                                Concept: The Sturges' formula is used to determine the number of classes for a frequency distribution:

                                \n\n

                                Formula: K = 1 + 3.322 × log10 N

                                \n\n

                                Where: K = Number of classes , N = Total number of observations

                                \n\n

                                Calculation:अवधारणा: स्टर्जेस का सूत्र बारंबारता बंटन के लिए वर्गों की संख्या निर्धारित करने के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है:

                                \n\n

                                सूत्र: K = 1 + 3.322 × log10 N

                                \n\n

                                जहाँ: K = वर्गों की संख्या, N = प्रेक्षणों की कुल संख्या

                                \n\n

                                गणना:

                                \n\n

                                1. दिए गए विकल्पों के अनुसार:

                                \n\n

                                विकल्प 1: 2 + 3.322 x log10 N (स्टर्जेस के सूत्र के अनुसार गलत है)

                                \n\n

                                विकल्प 2: 3 + 3.322 x log10 N (स्टर्जेस के सूत्र के अनुसार गलत है)

                                \n\n

                                विकल्प 3: 1 + 3.322 x log10 N (स्टर्जेस के सूत्र के अनुसार सही है)

                                \n\n

                                विकल्प 4: उपरोक्त में से कोई नहीं (गलत, क्योंकि विकल्प 3 सही है)

                                \n\n

                                ∴ सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है।
